summary: A narrator hides under bushes beside a porch, eavesdropping on Danny and Simon, who are discussing a plan involving security theatre and a meeting with local activists. Simon, a young man who sells weed to friends to pay rent, seems to have been coached by occupants of a black SUV that picked him up earlier. The narrator is wearing Jason's expensive spy-shirt, and cigarette ash and snow complicate the eavesdropping as Danny and Simon nearly notice the narrator. The excerpt is part 126 of a longer fiction work labeled Book 14.
one_line: A narrator eavesdrops under a porch on Danny and Simon as they plot a security-theatre scheme with local activists.
key_facts: Simon is described as old enough for the job and easily jammed up because he paid his rent by selling weed to his friends.
The narrator thinks Simon would choose helping stage security theatre over going to jail.
Someone in a black SUV picked Simon up in the afternoon and might have been coaching him for the meeting.
Danny gives Simon a slight nod, as if they had just made a private agreement.
Danny leaves through the front door saying he is going out for a smoke, and Simon follows shortly after holding a pack of cigarettes.
The narrator slips out the back door, circles the side of the house, and crawls under bushes along the foundation.
The narrator crawls between two clumps of spiky evergreen shrubs and straightens up beside the porch.
Cigarette ash lands on the sleeve of Jason's expensive spy-shirt, which the narrator brushes off hoping it left no hole.
Danny asks whether the others can be trusted, and he is told, "They're solid."
Someone leans over the wooden banister and asks, "You hear that?" and the narrator freezes.
Danny says it must have been a squirrel after a few seconds of silence.
Simon wheedles Danny by offering to set up what Danny needs.
Danny says, "Seriously, we need to get something real going."
Simon says, "They have the stuff, you have the skills. Boom," and then makes a joke about a pun.
Danny says he is happy if he can make connections.
